# dsh-crash-triage
**Turn one MLIR crash into a reproducible command, a minimal IR, the failing pass, a sanitizer stack
and a handoff report.**
English | 简体中文
One tool, `crash_triage`, four actions:
| action | what it does |

| `diagnose` (default) | reproduce → minimize with `mlir-reduce` → bisect passes → write report |
|

`reduce` | IR minimization only |
| `bisect` | find the first pass that crashes |
| `parse` | parse
a sanitizer report only — no `mlir-opt`, no reproduce/reduce/bisect |
The plugin never throws `ENOENT` at the model: missing tools, missing IR, out-of-workspace output di
rs, timeouts and cancellation all come back as `ok:false` with a Chinese `hint` and a `stage`.
## Not in scope (v1)
No core dumps, no symbolization (sanitizer reports are supplied by the caller), no automatic bug fix
ing, no compiling MLIR, no arbitrary shell. Only `mlir-opt`, `mlir-reduce` and the testers `node` ar
e spawned, always as argv arrays.
## Requirements

- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`
- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0-0`
- `mlir-opt` (required)

and `mlir-reduce` (minimization only); LLVM 23.1.4 is what this repo is verified against.
- `node` f
or the reducer tester is resolved by the plugin itself.
Without `mlir-reduce` the plugin still loads, but asking for minimization (the default) makes both `
diagnose` and `reduce` return `TOOL_NOT_FOUND`; pass `reduce: { enabled: false }` to diagnose withou
t it (reproduction + pass bisect still run).

## Tool `crash_triage`
Key parameters: `action`, `irPath` (resolved against `cwd`), `stdin` (inline IR text), `pipeline`, `
passList` (top-level passes; also the bisect split), `runnerArgs`, `cwd`, `env`, `timeoutMs`, `outpu
tDir` (must stay inside the session cwd), `keepWorkDir`, `sanitizer{ mode, reportPath, inline, maxFr
ames }`, `reduce{ enabled, maxIterations, maxTimeMs, maxCandidates, testArgs }`, `bisect{ enabled, m
axRuns, strategy, stopAtFirst }`, `report{ format, includeStderr }`.

`status` is one of `diagnosed` / `reduced` / `bisected` / `parsed` / `partial` / `failed`. `ok` is `
true` only when every requested stage succeeded; in `diagnose` a failed reduction still lets pass bi
sect run, and the result comes back as `ok:false, status:"partial"` with the earlier stages kept. A
single nested top-level pass yields `PASS_NESTED` the same way (`partial`, `bisect.attempted:false`)
ingle nested top-level pass yields `PASS_NESTED` the same way (`partial`, `bisect.attempted:false`).
Success shape: `{ ok, status, action, input{ irPath, sha256, pipeline }, crash{ reproduced, stable,
attempts, exitCode, kind, signature{ key }, sanitizer }, reducer{ attempted, ok, reductionPercent, o
utputPath }, bisect{ attempted, ok, failingPass, failingIndex, passingPrefix, evidence }, reproducer
{ command, text }, artifacts{ workDir, reportPath, ... }, warnings, hints }`. Failures carry `error{
code, message, hint, stage }` and still write `result.json` / `report.md`.
## Artifacts
`<workDir>/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>-<ir-name>/` contains `input.mlir`, `baseline.stdout.log`, `baseline.std
err.log`, `sanitizer.log`, `minimized.mlir` / `last-good.mlir`, `tester.log`, `reduce.log`, `passes.
log`, `reproducer.txt`, `result.json` and `report.md` (one-line conclusion, reproducer, input, crash
, minimal IR, failing pass, sanitizer stack, artifacts, next steps, warnings, hints).

## Limitations
Parse-stage crashes (e.g. very deep nesting) also crash @@mlir-reduce@@ itself before it ever calls
the tester, leaving an empty @@reduced.mlir@@ — reported as @@REDUCE_FAILED@@ (with mlir-reduce's ex
it code), not @@REDUCE_UNSTABLE@@. No symbolization; nested pipelines are not split (`func.func(a,b)
` counts as one top-level segment); `mlir-reduce` has no iteration cap so `maxIterations` / `maxCand
idates` only warn; the signature is derived from process output only; bisect uses prefix search plus
`print-ir` cross-check, and conflicting evidence is kept with a warning.
